metaTitle: Fence Cost in Dallas TX: Per-Foot Price Ranges by Source
metaDescription: Fence cost in Dallas: one DFW firm lists wood privacy at $15-$30/ft, another $38-$48/ft. See each source and what drives a quote. Call (214) 555-0137.
h1: Fence Cost in Dallas, TX: What Firms Publish Per Foot
heroSub: Wood, iron and gate prices from named Dallas-area firms, each kept as the range that firm publishes, plus the things that push a written quote up or down.
introHtml:
Search for fence cost in Dallas and you will not find one agreed number. One DFW firm publishes $15-$30 per linear foot for wood privacy fence installation, while Ergeon's Dallas County page lists wood fence at $38-$48 per foot installed. The gap is real, and it comes from what is in the price, the wood, the height and who is quoting.

White Rock Fence Co is advertising that connects Dallas homeowners with independent fence contractors. It does not build fences or give quotes. Every figure below is what one named firm advertises, or a national guide labeled as national, read in October 2026. To get a real number for your yard, call (214) 555-0137 and ask to be put in touch with a contractor who will quote the job in writing, then collect two or three comparable quotes.

sections.heading: Why Dallas fence prices do not line up
sections.html:
Contractor cost pages are marketing pages. Each one reflects that firm's wood, crew and the jobs it wants, and most do not say what the per-foot figure includes. TX Fence & Deck, for example, lists cedar privacy fence at $18-$28 per foot on one page and wood privacy fence at $15-$30 on another. The same firm's automatic gate pages also start at different figures.

That is why this page keeps every range with the firm that published it and never blends them into one 'average Dallas fence cost'. A midpoint of numbers from different firms, with different scopes, would be a number nobody is actually offering.

Ergeon's Dallas County page also shows how much the source matters. Its wood price of $38-$48 per foot sits well above the $15-$30 from TX Fence & Deck, and it is not clear whether the two quote the same scope. Use the ranges to sanity-check a quote, not to predict one.

sections.heading: What moves a fence quote up or down
sections.html:
A few choices do most of the work on a written quote for a new or replacement fence. Ask every contractor to price them the same way so the quotes can be compared. The fence installation page walks through each choice in more detail.

  • Wood. TX Fence & Deck lists 150 ft of pressure-treated pine at $2,200-$3,300 installed and western red cedar at $3,000-$4,500. Ask the quote to name the wood.
  • Style. Board-on-board overlaps the pickets so the fence stays solid. TX Fence & Deck says it adds $2-$5 per foot over a basic dog-ear fence, and DFW Fence Contractor says about 30 percent.
  • Height. Only national figures exist for 8 ft. Fixr (national) puts 150 ft at $4,500-$12,750 for 8 ft against $2,250-$6,000 for 6 ft. No Dallas firm's 8 ft per-foot price was found, so ask for 6 ft and 8 ft priced separately.
  • Posts and ground. Much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture. Ask what the quote specifies for posts and concrete, and whether slope or an alley changes the labor.
  • Old fence tear-out and haul-off. No Dallas figure was found. Ask the contractor to include it or list it as its own line.
  • Cap, trim and gates. Check whether a top cap, trim rail and any walk or drive gate are in the base price or added.

sections.heading: Gates, repairs and staining: the smaller jobs
sections.html:
Not every job is a whole fence. For repair work, Roof Raiders & Co, a Dallas firm, lists a single post pulled and reset with new concrete at $150-$400, board replacement at $25-$60 per board, and straightening a leaning 10 to 30 ft section at $300-$800. TX Fence & Deck lists storm damage repair at $300-$1,200. No Dallas service-call minimum was found. See fence repair in Dallas and gate repair for more.

Staining is a separate line. TX Fence & Deck gives two ranges for professional staining in DFW: $1.00-$2.50 per foot on one page and $1.50-$3.00 on another. If a quote includes stain, ask which coat and how many.

Automatic gates are the biggest swing. TX Fence & Deck says most residential automatic gate installations in the Dallas area run $3,500-$10,000, and Fixr puts the national range at $2,500-$5,500. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence. Iron fence buyers can compare per-foot ranges on the iron fence page.

sections.heading: Costs outside the per-foot price: permits, HOA and shared fences
sections.html:
The City of Dallas says a fence permit is required for fences over 4 ft in a front yard and over 6 ft everywhere else. We could not find a published Dallas fence permit fee, so ask the City. Dallas also asks for a contractor on the application, and some cities, including Dallas, Richardson and Irving, register fence contractors, so ask any contractor about city registration and proof of insurance. Rules differ in the suburbs, such as Plano, Garland and Richardson. Confirm height and permit rules with the City and your HOA before you sign.

HOA approval can change the build. Texas law limits what an association can ban, but in many HOAs the association can still control the type of fence, so get written approval first.

On a shared fence, Texas Law Help says that when both neighbors use a fence straddling the boundary line, both own it and share the cost of repairs and replacement. That is general information, not legal advice. Talk to your neighbor before the quotes arrive so the split is settled early.

faq.q: How much does a fence cost in Dallas?
faq.a: There is no single published figure. TX Fence & Deck says most wood privacy fence installation in the Dallas-Fort Worth area runs $15-$30 per linear foot, Ergeon's Dallas County page lists wood at $38-$48 per foot, and DFW Fence Contractor says roughly $30-$60 for a 6-ft wood privacy fence. Wood type, style, height and what the quote includes explain much of the gap, so get two or three written quotes.

faq.q: What does 150 feet of wood fence cost in Dallas?
faq.a: TX Fence & Deck lists 150 linear feet of pressure-treated pine at $2,200-$3,300 installed and western red cedar at $3,000-$4,500. Another page from that firm gives $2,700-$4,200 for cedar. King of Kings Fence lists $2,700-$5,250 for wood. These are advertised ranges, not quotes.

faq.q: Does an 8-foot fence cost much more than a 6-foot fence?
faq.a: The only figures found are national. Fixr lists 150 ft at $2,250-$6,000 for 6 ft and $4,500-$12,750 for 8 ft. No Dallas firm publishes an 8 ft per-foot price that we found, so ask contractors to price both heights. In Dallas a permit is required over 6 ft outside the front yard, so confirm with the City and your HOA.

faq.q: Does a Dallas fence need a permit, and what does it cost?
faq.a: The City of Dallas checklist says a fence permit is required over 4 ft in a front yard and over 6 ft in all other locations. We could not find a published Dallas fence permit fee. Contact the City of Dallas Planning & Development and your HOA before the work starts, and ask the contractor who pulls the permit.

faq.q: Who pays for a shared fence between neighbors in Texas?
faq.a: Texas Law Help says that if both neighbors use a fence straddling the boundary line, both own it and share the cost of repairing and replacing it. A fence wholly on one lot belongs to that owner. This is general information, not legal advice, so check your own situation.
